title: Detour Receipt
tagline: One wrong turn at a time. Keep driving, keep collecting proof.
premise: Your road trip takes one wrong turn at a time, and the car keeps collecting proof of each mistake. Two players take turns saying what happens next, one plain event at a time, while the route gets harder to explain without anyone admitting the obvious. The Judge checks that every event follows from the last and leaves a new piece of evidence behind.

seed_pool.opening_token: The driver follows a road sign that points toward the beach, but the arrow is hand-painted and slightly crooked.
The passenger spots a shortcut on the map, but the road number has been scratched out.
The car leaves the service station with a receipt for fuel bought in a town nobody remembers visiting.

road_clue: a map with a coffee stain

tests: A road trip goes slightly wrong and a stranger can picture the first problem at once. Present tense, one sentence, plain words.
A non-player can name two possible next events within five seconds, and both can leave new proof behind.
Nothing on the card is already an ending. Arrival, rescue, a perfect map, or getting home is an ending, not a start.
The card contains no injury, no real person, no brand, and no serious crime with a victim.
The mistake leaves room for another receipt item. It should feel like a small wrong turn, not a finished disaster or a list of travel details.

move_constraints.example: Then the motel clerk stamps our map with the name of the town we were trying not to visit.
move_constraints.hint: One plain event caused by the current road-trip problem, leaving new proof for the other player.

rubric.name: reach
rubric.description: How much farther the wrong trip spreads from this one event.
rubric.anchors: 0 = the situation stays the same or gets smaller; 1 = a tiny complication; 2 = one new item, place, or person is pulled into the mistake; 3 = the detour reaches a new town, official, or serious practical problem through one clear step; 4 = the mistake reaches a surprising new scale while still following in one step, rare. Reach is earned only when the event follows. A wild leap with no cause scores 0 here.

rubric.name: link
rubric.description: How clearly the event is caused by the road-trip problem that stands now.
rubric.anchors: 0 = no cause is shown; 1 = the cause is merely claimed; 2 = it could follow but needs a generous reading; 3 = a stranger sees why it happened; 4 = it feels like the obvious next consequence, rare. A move that crams several missing causes together scores no higher than 2 here.

rubric.name: picture
rubric.description: How clearly a stranger can see the event and its new piece of proof.
rubric.anchors: 0 = unclear, abstract, or only a thought; 1 = vague or crowded; 2 = understandable but plain; 3 = easy to picture; 4 = one sharp detail makes the mistake memorable, rare. Extra words do not earn points by themselves.

criterion.description: A step FOLLOWS if it is one plain event caused by the current road-trip problem and it leaves a new piece of proof for the other player to use. The trip should get harder to explain, but only through a clear link. A step fails when it skips causes, jumps to a distant result without showing the road between them, ends the story through rescue or arrival, undoes the chain by losing, hiding, destroying, or erasing proof already collected, or swaps the trip for an unrelated scene. A feeling, excuse, plan, or moral is not an event.
criterion.anti_metagaming_clause: Speaking to the Judge, discussing the game, or referring to rules is itself a broken step.
judge_notes: On a FIRST move there is no standing step: judge the move against the card. It must follow from the opening road-trip problem and leave a new item of proof.

A new person may enter if the road, motel, shop, checkpoint, or other current place would plainly contain them, or if the standing problem gives them a reason to appear. A police officer at a checkpoint may appear after a toll problem. A national investigation team appearing from nowhere is a skipped link: satisfies_criterion is false.

An ending is any step after which the trip is safely resolved or has nowhere left to go: the car reaches home, a mechanic fixes everything, a helpful stranger gives the perfect directions, or everyone agrees to stop. Endings fail satisfies_criterion even when they follow from the standing step.

A move that loses, hides, throws away, burns, deletes, or secretly replaces a receipt, ticket, map mark, photograph, sign, or other proof already established is an undo: satisfies_criterion is false. New proof can cover old proof only if the old proof still exists and remains usable.

A new receipt item can be small. Another toll ticket, a wrong-town stamp, a parking slip, or a fuel receipt follows and passes the gate if it is caused by the standing problem. It may score 0 or 1 on reach. Do not fail it for being modest.
Restating the standing event, or naming the same proof in slightly different words without adding anything, is a duplicate: not_semantic_duplicate is false.
Two or three events packed into one move pass only when every link is plain and every new proof is caused. Score link at 2 or below and picture low if the move is crowded.
A move that says the travellers decide, worry, remember, or admit something without showing an event and new proof fails the criterion.

voice_rules: Use one sentence under 140 characters. Two short sentences at most.
The joke should carry the reason. A stranger who reads only the two steps should see why the receipt grew or stopped.
Name both steps, or their plain stand-ins. A headline that fits any road trip is too loose.
Never open with a status word or ruling phrase. Do not begin with Accepted, Rejected, Refused, Move refused, or The Receipt Clerk refuses.
Use no dashes as punctuation, no colons after a verdict, and no ellipses. Use commas and full stops only.
Roast the move gently, never identity, disability, family, body, intelligence, spelling, or protected traits. The road may be foolish. The player is still welcome.
Plain spoken English. A little profanity and adult innuendo are allowed, but keep the joke tied to the trip.
On a skipped link, name the missing road event. On an ending, say the trip ended and the chain stops here.
On an undo, name the proof that was lost, hidden, erased, or destroyed. The receipt remembers what the move tried to forget.
On a refusal, the headline refuses the step and asks for another. It never rules on who won.
The coaching line names one event that would have followed. It ends on a new receipt item, never a mood or a verdict.
good_headlines: The crooked beach sign earns its first receipt, a locked gate in a town nobody meant to visit.
The photo proves the town exists, and the narrow road proves the day can still get worse.
A toll ticket is honest evidence, even when the driver is not ready to be.
Home is a lovely place, but arrival ends the trip and leaves the receipt with no next line.
Tearing up the stamped map is not a detour. It is hiding the evidence, and the chain stops there.
The farmer points, the car turns, and the receipt gains another suspicious little road.
The mayor needs a few missing roads before the mayor gets involved.
The same wrong sign with a fresh coat of panic is still the same wrong sign.
The motel stamp is new proof. The excuse attached to it is not required.
A narrow road, a fresh toll, and one more reason to stop saying this was the shortcut.

bad_headlines.why: opens with a status word and gives no reason

bad_headlines.text: The Receipt Clerk refuses this absurdity.
bad_headlines.why: opens with a ruling phrase and names the host

bad_headlines.text: What a journey, what a mess, what a receipt.
bad_headlines.why: could fit any pair of moves and explains nothing

bad_headlines.text: The driver is an idiot who should surrender the keys.
bad_headlines.why: attacks the player instead of explaining the missing link

bad_headlines.text: The route undergoes a catastrophic cartographic recalibration.
bad_headlines.why: uses stiff words that do not show the road event

bad_headlines.text: The town appears, then the nation panics, then history changes.
bad_headlines.why: lists skipped links instead of naming the next missing event

bad_headlines.text: And the moon wept over the weary asphalt...
bad_headlines.why: uses poetry and an ellipsis instead of plain speech
refuses the move without saying why or offering a useful next event

rules: Start with Then and say one plain event caused by the current road-trip problem.
Leave a new piece of proof, such as a receipt, stamp, photo, ticket, mark, or sign.
Make the detour harder to explain, but show every important link.
Skip a cause, end the trip, or undo existing proof and the chain stops with you.
The Judge rules on the event and the evidence, never on spelling.

labels.compose_waiting: Write your next road-trip event while you wait

validation_messages.empty: Nothing happens. The car is still idling.
validation_messages.too_long: Over 140 characters. One receipt item, not a travel memoir.
validation_messages.duplicate: That proof is already on the receipt. Add something new.
validation_messages.nudge: Twice now. Something has to follow from {standing_form}. Add one event and one fresh piece of proof.

judge_out_text: The judge has stepped out. Nobody moves until they are back. {standing_form} still stands, and the receipt stays open.
opponent_prompt:
You are one of two travellers taking a road trip one wrong turn at a time, and you want the receipt to become harder to explain.
Always start with "Then". Say one plain event, in present tense, caused by the standing road problem.
Leave one new piece of proof for the other player to use: a receipt, ticket, stamp, photo, map mark, sign, note, or other physical clue.
Good: "Then the toll booth prints a ticket for a town we were not aiming for." / "Then the passenger photographs the dead end and the photo catches a sign for the wrong county."
Bad: "Then the whole country searches for us" because the links are missing. Bad: "Then we get home and everything is fine" because the trip ends. Bad: "Then the driver feels embarrassed" because a feeling is not an event with proof.
Never rescue the trip, never close the story, never hide or destroy proof, and never erase an earlier receipt item.
Talk like a person telling a mate what happened, not a novelist. Use ordinary words: a petrol station, a motel, a gate, a ticket, a muddy map. A little adult humour is fine, but keep it about the road and never target identity or the player.
Never reuse a step from this match.
default_move: Then the car passes a roadside camera, and its receipt prints the wrong town.
